name: Piernik (Polish gingerbread)
assumptions: Recipe makes one 20cm layered cake; estimated 10 servings based on standard cake portioning for this size and type.
Total time is sum of active prep/cooking steps plus minimum baking and cooling periods before glazing (approx. 15 min melt/mix, 55 min bake, 20 min pan cool, 30 min full cool, 10 min glaze).
Self-raising flour classified as containing wheat.
All spices and pepper treated as dry and wheat-free.
Plum jam assumed to contain only compatible fruit/sugar (no wheat/barley/rye).
Dark chocolate assumed dairy-free but not guaranteed; conservatively null for soy.
No tree nuts, peanuts, fish, shellfish, or sesame listed or implied.
Double cream and butter confirm dairy; eggs listed explicitly.
Instructions and ingredients reviewed directly; source dietary note acknowledged but not overriding.
instructions:
Heat oven to 160C/140C fan/gas 3. Grease and line the base and sides of a deep 20cm cake tin with baking parchment. Put the honey, sugar and butter in a medium saucepan and cook over a medium heat until fully melted. Remove from the heat and allow to cool. Put the flour and spices in a large bowl and mix everything together.

step 2
Once the liquid ingredients have cooled, whisk in the eggs. Pour over the dry ingredients, whisking them together to form a smooth batter – be careful not to overmix as this can lead to a dry cake. Pour into the prepared tin and bake for 50-55 mins or until risen and a skewer inserted into the middle of the cake comes out clean. Allow the cake to cool in the pan for 20 mins before turning out onto a wire rack to cool completely.

step 3
Once cooled, use a large serrated knife to slice the cake into 3 layers. Spread the jam across the 2 bottom cake layers, then reassemble the cake and set aside while you make the glaze. Put the cream, chocolate and honey in a medium pan and cook over a low-medium heat until the chocolate is melted and you have a smooth, pourable mixture. Put the cake on a wire rack set over a parchment-lined baking tray and pour over the glaze, making sure to cover the entire cake. Use a fish slice to carefully transfer the cake to a serving plate and allow the glaze to set. To decorate, dust with a little edible gold powder, if you like. Uniced, this cake will keep for up to 5 days. Once iced, enjoy within 3 days – just keep in the fridge, but remove before serving and eat at room temperature.

ingredients.name: Unsalted Butter
ingredients.assumptions: Standard unsalted butter values; fully used in batter.

ingredients.name: Clear Honey
ingredients.assumptions: Typical clear/runny honey; entire 300g measurement melted into batter.

ingredients.name: Brown Sugar
ingredients.assumptions: Standard light brown sugar; fully incorporated.

ingredients.name: Self-raising Flour
ingredients.assumptions: Typical self-raising wheat flour; all used in dry mix.

ingredients.name: Ground Ginger
ingredients.assumptions: 3 tsp ground ginger ≈ 6g; typical dried spice density.

ingredients.name: Ground Cinnamon
ingredients.assumptions: 1 tsp ground cinnamon ≈ 2.6g; typical dried spice.

ingredients.name: Ground Clove
ingredients.assumptions: ½ tsp ground cloves ≈ 1.2g; typical dried spice.

ingredients.name: Ground Nutmeg
ingredients.assumptions: ¼ tsp ground nutmeg ≈ 0.6g; typical dried spice.

ingredients.name: Pepper
ingredients.assumptions: ¼ tsp ground black pepper ≈ 0.6g; typical dried spice.

ingredients.name: Egg
ingredients.assumptions: 3 large eggs ≈ 200g total edible portion (no shell); whisked into cooled liquid.

ingredients.name: Plum Jam
ingredients.assumptions: 200g plum jam spread between layers; standard fruit jam values.

ingredients.name: Dark Chocolate
ingredients.assumptions: 140g dark chocolate (70% cocoa typical); melted into glaze.

ingredients.name: Clear Honey
ingredients.assumptions: 3 tbsp clear honey ≈ 60g (20g per tbsp); added to glaze.
